sourcedFrom: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code (ABSENT)
cleanIntro: Christensen's own book for the Modern Carbon Rifle. The strip is short — magazine, bolt, and if you are going further, the barrelled action out of the stock — and the bolt release is the only part that is not obvious: it must be held fully depressed or the bolt will not clear the action. Two things about this rifle are worth carrying in your head before you start. The barrel is carbon-fibre wrapped over a stainless liner, and the manual bans graphite lubricants outright because graphite encourages corrosion. And the action screws have a stated torque — 65 inch-pounds — so the barrelled action should not come out of the stock unless you have a wrench to put it back properly.

steps.title: Safety back to S
steps.action: The safety lever sits to the right of the bolt shroud on a right-handed rifle. Move it all the way back to the S position before anything else. Note the rifle's own quirk here: if it is not cocked, the lever will not go to safe at all — an owner who meets that is not fighting a broken safety, he is holding an uncocked rifle.
steps.aside: Your safety lever is located to the right of the bolt shroud (right-handed rifles). The safety mechanism provides some degree of protection from accidental or unintentional discharge under normal usage when properly engaged and in good working condition.
steps.quote: To engage the safety, move the safety lever all the way back to the “S” position.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — SAFETY FEATURES, printed p.5

steps.title: Magazine out before the bolt comes back
steps.action: Push the magazine catch lever forward and draw the magazine down. Do this BEFORE you open the bolt: with rounds still in the magazine, working the bolt to check the chamber simply feeds another one. Christensen spells that consequence out, and it is the single most dangerous order-of-operations mistake on a box-fed bolt rifle.
steps.aside: WARNING: IF THE CARTRIDGE IN THE MAGAZINE OR MAG BOX ARE NOT REMOVED PRIOR TO THIS PROCEDURE, ANY ROUNDS LEFT IN IT WILL BE CHAMBERED, WHICH COULD LEAD TO AN UNINTENTIONAL DISCHARGE. THE RIFLE WILL FIRE WITH A ROUND CHAMBERED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pushing the magazine catch lever forward and pulling the magazine down.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.15

steps.title: Catch the magazine — it drops free
steps.action: Keep a hand under the magazine as the lever goes forward. It falls free rather than staying put, and a dropped magazine landing on concrete is how feed lips get bent out of true.
steps.quote: CAUTION: THE MAGAZINE MAY FALL FREE WHEN THE MAGAZINE CATCH LEVER IS PRESSED. DON’T ALLOW THE MAGAZINE TO FALL ONTO A HARD SURFACE. DOING SO MAY DAMAGE THE MAGAZINE.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.15

steps.title: Bolt back, chamber checked
steps.action: Now open the bolt and let it pull any chambered round out. With the magazine gone and the bolt back, look into the chamber and confirm it is empty. This is the manual's own clearing order — safety, magazine, then bolt and chamber.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT: Put the safety selector in the “SAFE” position. Remove the magazine, THEN pull the bolt back and check the chamber.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — CLEARING THE RIFLE, printed p.17

steps.title: Unloaded, and eye protection on
steps.action: Christensen asks for safety glasses for disassembly, not just for shooting — there are springs under tension in the bolt and the magazine, and solvent gets flicked about during cleaning.
steps.aside: WARNING: ALWAYS UNLOAD YOUR FIREARM BEFORE CLEANING, LUBRICATION, DISASSEMBLY OR REASSEMBLY.
steps.quote: WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN DISASSEMBLING, MAINTAINING OR ASSEMBLING YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.17

steps.title: Bolt handle up, all the way back
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction, confirm again that it is not loaded, then lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt fully rearward until it stops. It must be at the very back for the release to let it out.
steps.quote: Lift Bolt Handle and pull all the way back.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — REMOVE BOLT ASSEMBLY, printed p.17

steps.title: Hold the bolt release FULLY down and slide the bolt out
steps.action: Depress the bolt release completely and hold it there while you slide the bolt out of the rifle. 'Fully' is the operative word — a half-pressed release lets the bolt move an inch and then stop dead, and people take that for an obstruction and start pulling. Keep it held down and the bolt comes straight out.
steps.quote: While depressing Bolt Release fully, slide the Bolt from the Rifle.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — REMOVE BOLT ASSEMBLY, printed p.17

steps.title: Look through the bore while it is open
steps.action: With the bolt out you have a clear view down the barrel from the breech. Take it — check for obstructions or debris now, because this is the only moment in the strip where the bore is visible end to end. A patch or a lodged bullet found here is a cleaning job; found later it is a wrecked barrel.
steps.quote: Check the barrel for any obstructions or debris by visually inspecting the bore.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete — the stock only comes off if you must
steps.action: Bolt out and magazine out is the working strip, and it is all the routine clean needs. Christensen does publish taking the barrelled action out of the stock, and Deep Clean below covers it — but that means undoing the action screws, and they go back at a stated torque. Do not take the stock off casually.
steps.quote: Remove the action screws 08] Remove the barreled action from the stock assembly.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — REMOVING BARRELED ACTION, printed p.17

deepSteps.title: Barrelled action out — only with a torque wrench to hand
deepSteps.action: With the bolt already out and the rifle confirmed empty, back out the action screws and lift the barrelled action from the stock. Do not start this unless you can put it back at the figure Christensen gives: 65 inch-pounds. Action screws set by feel are the usual cause of a rifle that will not hold zero afterwards.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the action screws 08] Remove the barreled action from the stock assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — REMOVING BARRELED ACTION, printed p.17

deepSteps.title: Chamber and locking lugs — brush, push and twist
deepSteps.action: Put a chamber brush on the rod, wet it with solvent and work it into the chamber and the locking lug recesses, pushing and twisting rather than just stroking. The lug recesses are where fouling hides on a bolt gun and where it does the most harm to consistent lock-up.
deepSteps.quote: Install the chamber brush on the cleaning rod, dip it in cleaning solvent and insert into the chamber and locking lugs. Clean by pushing and twisting the cleaning rod.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Bore from the breech, and never reverse the brush
deepSteps.action: Always push the patch or brush in from the breech end, following the bullet. And once a bore brush is in the bore it goes all the way through before it comes back — reversing direction mid-bore is capitalised as a caution twice in this manual, because dragging the bristles backwards over the rifling is how they get torn out and lodged.
deepSteps.aside: CAUTION: DO NOT REVERSE THE DIRECTION OF THE BORE BRUSH WHILE IT IS IN THE BORE.
deepSteps.quote: ALWAYS push the cleaning/oiling patch from the breech end.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — CLEANING, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: Solvents — anything but graphite
deepSteps.action: Use a good solvent for metal fouling and lubricate generously, but read the one absolute ban in this book: no lubricant containing graphite, under any condition, because graphite encourages rapid corrosion in this rifle. Check the label of any dry-film or 'moly-graphite' product before it goes near the action.
deepSteps.quote: Under NO condition should any lubricant containing graphite be used with your rifle. Graphite can encourage rapid corrosion in your rifle.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — CLEANING SOLVENTS AND LUBRICANTS, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: Light oil on bore, chamber, barrel and lugs
deepSteps.action: Lightly lubricate the bore, the chamber and the outside of the barrel, and put oil on the locking lugs. Light is the word — Christensen warns elsewhere that preservative left in the bore raises pressure, so anything you leave in there has to come out with a dry patch before the rifle is fired.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly lubricate the bore, chamber and outer surface of the barrel. 09] With a lubricated swab, run the rod from the receiver to the muzzle brake (if applicable). Do not over lubricate. 10] Lubricate the locking lugs.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Do not swap bolts, and wash your hands
deepSteps.action: If you own more than one rifle, keep each bolt with its own action — the manual capitalises this and it is a headspace matter, not housekeeping. And the fouling you have just brushed out contains lead; wash before you eat or smoke.
deepSteps.aside: WARNING: LEAD MAY BE PRESENT IN THE FOULING OF A DIRTY RIFLE. AVOID CONTACT WITH IT AND CLEAN HANDS AFTERWARD TO AVOID INGESTING LEAD.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! DO NOT INTERCHANGE BOLTS BETWEEN RIFLES.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Back together: thread locker, then 65 inch-pounds
deepSteps.action: Reapply thread-locking compound to the screws as you go back together, and torque the action screws to 65 inch-pounds. Then put the bolt in: the two front lugs are not identical — one is grooved and one is not — and the grooves have to match the action's. The firing pin collar should end up resting in the detent at the top of the cocking ramp.
deepSteps.aside: Simply insert the bolt into the action. At the front of the bolt there are two lugs. One has a groove and one does not. Match up the grooves on the lug with the grooves on the action. The firing pin collar should be resting in the detent location at the top of the cocking ramp.
deepSteps.quote: Reapply thread-locking compound to all screws.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — REASSEMBLY, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Functional check — both halves
deepSteps.action: Magazine out, chamber checked by eye and by hand, then an empty magazine in to confirm the catch holds it, and out again. Safety to SAFE and squeeze: the firing pin must NOT fall. Safety to FIRE and squeeze: it must fall. Fail either half and Christensen wants a phone call, not a fix at the bench.
deepSteps.aside: Place the safety in the “FIRE” position. Squeeze the trigger and hold the trigger to the rear; the firing pin should fall.
deepSteps.quote: Place the safety in the “SAFE” position. Squeeze the trigger. The firing pin should not fall.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Carbon Rifle Owner's Manual — undated — the book carries no revision code — FUNCTIONAL CHECK, printed p.20

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bolt and magazine out; rifle on its side, ejection port up, or upright in a vise
Correct-calibre brush on the rod, wetted in solvent, pushed through from the BREECH end
Several passes, never reversing the brush while it is in the bore
Patches on the jag, a clean one each time, until they come out clean
One oiled patch through, then a dry patch to take the excess back out

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & LUGS
tasks: Chamber brush dipped in solvent, pushed and twisted into the chamber and locking lugs
Let solvent stand on heavy carbon, then wipe clean
Light lubricant on the locking lugs

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe the bolt body down and inspect the face
Light lubricant on the moving surfaces — no graphite, ever
Never fit another rifle's bolt to this action

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Stock wiped with a damp rag, warm water or mild household cleaner
Barrel wiped with gun oil and dried back to restore the finish
Inspect barrel and stock for cracks, bends or breaks, and the bore for obstructions
If a muzzle brake is fitted, clean the baffles while cleaning the rifle

reassembly: Reapply thread-locking compound to all screws as they go back.
Torque the action screws to 65 inch-pounds — the figure is the manual's, and guessing it costs accuracy.
Insert the bolt into the action matching the grooved lug to the groove in the action; the firing pin collar rests in the detent at the top of the cocking ramp.
If the comb or length of pull was moved, check the comb latches positively into its locked position before the rifle goes away.
Run the functional check, both halves, before you call it done.
fncheck: Remove the magazine and check the chamber by eye and by hand. Fit an empty magazine and confirm the catch holds it solidly, then take it out again. With the safety in the SAFE position, squeeze the trigger — the firing pin must not fall. Move the safety to FIRE, squeeze and hold the trigger to the rear — the firing pin must fall. If the rifle fails either test, Christensen's instruction is to call them rather than to adjust anything yourself.
